title: Globalisation and the Internet Age

cards.h: A steel box and a web page changed how the world trades and talks
cards.b:
In 1956 a trucker named Malcolm McLean loaded 58 metal containers onto a ship in New Jersey. It sounds dull. It made shipping so cheap that making a shirt in one country and selling it in another became normal.

Then, in 1989-91, a scientist at CERN gave us the Web.
After the Cold War, trade barriers fell. The WTO started in 1995. China joined in December 2001 and became the 'world's factory'.

The Internet existed before the Web. Tim Berners-Lee, at CERN in Switzerland, proposed the World Wide Web in 1989 and it opened to the public in 1991. Google appeared in 1998 and Facebook in 2004.

Smartphones, from 2007, put the Internet in billions of pockets.

Globalisation lifted hundreds of millions out of poverty, especially in Asia. But many factory workers in rich countries lost jobs, and inequality grew in many places.

The 2008 financial crisis, then Brexit (2016) and trade wars, led many to ask if globalisation was going into reverse. Some call the new phase 'slowbalisation'.

Films, music, food and memes cross borders in seconds. Data became the new oil, and a few big firms hold a lot of it. Questions about privacy, misinformation and who controls the networks are now political issues.

Myth: the world only got connected recently.Fact: the Silk Road, Indian Ocean trade and the Columbian Exchange were global. The 19th century saw a huge wave of trade too, which ended with World War I. What is new is the speed and the digital layer.

Reform, IT and UPI

The 1991 reforms opened India to the world. Software firms like Infosys, founded in Bangalore in 1981, found a market in Y2K work in the late 1990s. India became a major exporter of IT services.

In 2016 Jio made mobile data cheap. In April 2016 the National Payments Corporation of India launched UPI, which lets anyone send money from a phone. By 2023 it handled more than 10 billion transactions a month.

Aadhaar, the ID system begun in 2009, made opening a bank account and signing up for a phone far easier, so millions went digital without ever holding a credit card.

Five things to remember

  1. Containers made trade cheap (1956).
  2. The Web went public in 1991.
  3. The WTO began in 1995; China joined in 2001.
  4. Gains were uneven.
  5. India's IT and digital payments rose after 1991.

Think about it

  • What do we lose if supply chains shrink?
  • Who should control data?
